summary: Iteration 4 (hero redesign + 4-poster reseed) full backend + frontend regression. Backend 47/47 pytest PASS after aligning 3 seed-dependent assertions (product count 12 -> 4, Tokyo Nights -> Spider-Man for slug/final_price check, search q 'tokyo' -> 'spider'). No production code changes; only test data expectations were updated to reflect the deliberate seed replacement. All 4 seeded products (Spider-Man/movies, Tanjiro/anime, Ferrari Formula 1/cars, Vogue Leopard/fashion) verified via GET /api/products with images all pointing to customer-assets-jai6qajn.emergentagent.net. GET /api/settings returns hero_background_url set to in0gb79z_image.png. Categories now include anime, cars, sports, movies, music, fashion, gaming, cities, motivational, keychains (10). Frontend: Hero renders user's uploaded collector-room image via (object-cover, objectPosition center 40%), full-bleed, dark overlay at 28% baseline. Headline 'COLLECT WHAT YOU LOVE.' rendered uppercase, font-weight 900, 'LOVE.' visibly orange (rgb(255,106,0) via CSS variable). Subheading exact copy 'Premium posters and acrylic keychains inspired by anime, sports, cars, music and pop culture. Curate your walls. Express your personality.' present. Two CTAs testid=hero-shop-btn -> /shop?type=posters and testid=hero-keychains-btn -> /shop?type=keychains. At 1440x900 the hero-shop-btn rect is top=779 bottom=829 (vh=900) — fits within 100vh, no scroll needed. Nav inner container height = 68px (h-14 md:h-[68px]). Exactly 3 nav-link testids: home, shop, about. Nav bg at scrollY=0 = rgba(10,10,10,0) (transparent); at scrollY=500 = rgba(10,10,10,0.7) with backdrop-filter blur — glass transition works. Home Featured Posters section renders exactly 4 real product cards (product-card-spider-man / -tanjiro / -ferrari-formula-1 / -vogue-leopard) using the user-uploaded images. 'Why Paper & Loop' shows Premium Paper, Museum Quality Print, Fade Resistant, High Resolution. 'Acrylic Keychains — coming soon' section renders as CTA card (no fake products). Customer Gallery renders seeded gallery items (brand imagery). Shop page: default lists all 4 posters; type=Posters -> all 4; theme=Anime -> only Tanjiro; theme=Cars -> only Ferrari; theme=Movies -> only Spider-Man; theme=Keychains type -> empty state 'Nothing here yet' (correct — no keychain products in DB). Zero console errors across Home and Shop.

issues: Shop.jsx TAXONOMY.posters.themes lacks 'Fashion' (and 'Cities'). Vogue Leopard (category_slug=fashion) is therefore only discoverable via the type=Posters + theme=All view; no dedicated Fashion theme chip surfaces it. The product IS accessible (not hidden), but the drill-down UX is inconsistent with the seeded fashion category. Add 'Fashion' and 'Cities' theme entries to TAXONOMY.posters.themes in /app/frontend/src/pages/Shop.jsx to match the backend's category set.

<Nav> is sticky top-0 rather than fixed / absolute overlaying the hero. At scrollY=0 the nav takes its own 68px of layout space above the hero image (visible as a strip between announcement bar and hero). Nav backgroundColor is correctly transparent (rgba(10,10,10,0)) so the request 'transparent over hero' evaluates true only in scroll-back state. If the intent is a true full-bleed hero (image starts at top of viewport with nav floating over it), switch <motion.header> from `sticky` to `fixed inset-x-0 top-0` and add top-padding to the hero section by height of announcement bar + 68px. Reporting for E1 decision — this is a design/positioning choice, not a broken behaviour.

action_items: Add 'Fashion' (slug: fashion) and optionally 'Cities' theme entries to TAXONOMY.posters.themes in /app/frontend/src/pages/Shop.jsx so Vogue Leopard (and future Cities posters) get a first-class theme chip.
Decide whether nav should truly overlay the hero (fixed + hero top padding) or the current sticky-above-hero layout is intended.
critical_code_review_comments: Home.jsx Hero uses `settings?.hero_background_url` with an inline URL fallback constant. If the settings API fails or is slow the hardcoded fallback still ships the correct user image — good defensive default, but the fallback duplicates the URL. Consider centralising in /app/frontend/src/lib/media.js as DEFAULT_HERO_BG for reuse.

server.py seed_if_empty relies on db.settings['seed_flags'].user_products_seeded to prevent re-seed. Please confirm the flag is set atomically in the same migration that inserted the 4 products — otherwise a fresh empty DB + missing flag would re-inject the old 12 stock products.

Shop.jsx themeFor() still uses keyword-based bucketing over product names/descriptions; without an explicit product.theme field, a poster named e.g. 'Naruto Rasengan' would need the keyword 'anime' somewhere in metadata to land in the Anime chip. Consider adding a `theme` field to the Product model (backwards-compatible optional) so admins can bucket products explicitly.

backend_test.py TestHealth::test_products_seeded and TestProducts::test_search_q / test_get_by_slug_computed are now tightly coupled to the 4-poster seed. Any future seed change will require another test update — acceptable for a curated store but worth flagging.
SettingsUpdate model expansion with hero_background_url worked cleanly via PUT /api/admin/settings (verified indirectly through GET /api/settings returning the field).
